look_here_first: LOOK FIRST at a FULLY MATURE spikelet: C. odoratus is unusual because a corky, winged spikelet RACHILLA disarticulates into one-fruited segments (each includes a scale, rachilla internode and achene). Usually subcylindrical spikelets; brown head color is secondary, not diagnostic.

key_traits.label: Habit
key_traits.text: Annual or short-lived perennial in muddy wetland margins, shores or disturbed moist places, with large spreading leaflike terminal bracts.

key_traits.label: Inflorescence
key_traits.text: Umbel-like branching rays with headlets and elongated narrow spikelets, often rust-colored but variable.

key_traits.label: Spikelets
key_traits.text: Cylindrical or subcylindrical maturity. Corky winged rachilla breaks at each scale into one-fruited segments; this is key.

key_traits.label: Scales
key_traits.text: Disarticulating rachilla internode bears its floral scale and achene, not merely scales falling individually.

key_traits.label: Fruit
key_traits.text: Single achene per reduced flower; achene may remain clasped by a corky winged one-fruited rachilla segment.
